description: github-actions manager disabled: GitHub Dependabot manages hort's .github/workflows; Renovate handles the cargo / docker / gitlab-ci deps and targets develop. NOTE: Renovate reads this from the default branch (main), so it takes effect once this reaches main via a develop->main promotion.

packageRules.description: Keep sha2/hmac/md-5/sha1 on one RustCrypto generation: hort's own code unifies all four through a single digest major at two compile-enforced sites, so one of them moving alone cannot build. crates/hort-http-maven/src/sidecar.rs boxes sha1::Sha1, md5::Md5 and sha2::Sha256/Sha512 behind one Box<dyn DynDigest>, and that trait is sha2's re-export of digest, so sha1 and md-5 must implement the very same one; crates/hort-notifier-webhook/src/lib.rs builds Hmac::<Sha256> for the webhook body signature, which pins hmac to sha2's digest major too. Measured, not assumed: Cargo.lock has sha2 0.11.0, md-5 0.11.0, sha1 0.11.0 and hmac 0.13.0 all on digest 0.11.3. This is structural, not the old mid-flight-migration hold - that migration landed and the coupling outlived it. The graph's second line, digest 0.10.7, is transitive-only (crc-fast under object_store, sqlx-core, and the sigstore/openidconnect stack are all still on the 0.10 generation) plus the sigstore adapter's own sha2 0.10 requirement, documented on the dependency block of crates/hort-adapters-provenance-sigstore/Cargo.toml; every other workspace manifest asks for the 0.11 set, so that line is not what this rule holds. Unpark when a move of all four to the next digest generation is deliberately scheduled as one coordinated change.

Hold quick-xml below 0.42: 0.42 makes text decoding infallible, which breaks the Maven readers' fallible-decode invariant (decode_text in crates/hort-formats/src/maven/xml.rs returns None on invalid UTF-8 so an unneeded element cannot abort the reader); and while object_store still requires quick-xml ^0.41, a bump splits the graph across both versions. Unpark when object_store's own quick-xml requirement reaches 0.42.

Hold x509-cert and const-oid at the majors the sigstore crate compiles against. The type-unification coupling that forces this is documented at length on the dependency block of crates/hort-adapters-provenance-sigstore/Cargo.toml - read it there; it is deliberately not restated here. Unpark when a sigstore release itself moves to x509-cert 0.3 / der 0.8.

Hold cvss below 3.0: 3.0 removes or renames cvss::v3::Base - measured, not assumed (test:lint fails with 'cannot find type Base in module cvss::v3') - and both call sites, crates/hort-adapters-scanner-osv/src/severity.rs and crates/hort-adapters-advisory-osv/src/severity.rs, parse a CVSS v3 vector into the base score that drives severity classification, which is what the scan-policy gates act on. 2.2.0 carries no advisory, so the bump buys nothing functional while costing a port on the path that decides what gets quarantined. Unlike the other holds here this one waits on no upstream: unpark when the port is deliberately scheduled, or when an advisory against 2.2.0 forces it.

Cap hyper-util at 0.1.20 until the instance can serve 0.1.21 again. 0.1.21 is scan-rejected on the dogfood registry over an advisory about a component that is not in the crate: a cargo SBOM is built from the published .crate's embedded Cargo.lock, which is the foreign maintainer's dev resolve, so a finding about h2 0.4.13 condemned hyper-util itself. The narrowing that fixes it is commit 39b3a447 (a finding may condemn only an artifact that carries the named component) and it is in no published release yet - so a release build resolving through the proxy cannot see 0.1.21, while the fix can only reach the instance through such a build. 0.1.20 breaks that cycle: it is the version the last final release carried, so the proxy already holds it released, and the requirement is ^0.1 so the cap needs no manifest change. Unpark once a release carrying 39b3a447 runs on the instance AND a rescan has released 0.1.21 there - verify by requesting the version through the proxy, not by assuming the rescan ran.

Resolve crate versions through hort's crates-proxy sparse index instead of crates.io: the pull-through proxy that fires the on_dist_tag_move prefetch on each index read, warming the newest versions off the build's critical path. (cargo-virtual is the CI build source but aggregates crates-proxy, and its serve-path is still in progress, so crates-proxy is the reliable trigger point; warmed content lives here regardless.) Auth (hostRules matchHost hort.kdp.kloni.cloud, hostType crate, plus a hort read token) comes from the renovate-runner; this repo config carries only the routing. Note: crates-proxy uses indexMode include_pending, so not-yet-warmed upstream versions are visible — the read starts the quarantine clock early but does not guarantee a proposed version is released by the first build's fetch. Renovate's supplementary /api/v1/crates/ metadata probe 404s on hort (non-fatal noise, thinner changelog).

The tested Postgres version window is a deliberate policy decision, not an automatic bump: the floor is tested in the every-push CI tier, the newest supported version runs in the locally-invocable tiers. The window moves only when that decision is revisited.
The tested Redis version is a deliberate policy decision, not an automatic bump.
The helm tooling image is updated only when needed, not automatically on every major.
